top_news.title: AI agents build 3D scenes from photos but have no idea if they got it right
top_news.dek: LEGO-Anything converts single images into editable Blender code, though agents struggle to verify geometric accuracy.
top_news.brief: The LEGO-Anything framework uses a coding agent to generate executable Blender scripts from single photos, allowing for scene editing and analysis. While effective at reconstruction, benchmarks show that current agents lack the ability to self-evaluate the geometric accuracy of their output, performing no better than random chance.
top_news.image_alt: LEGO-Anything overview showing code generation from a single photo

top_news.title: Show HN: Made an open-source Lego AI generator
top_news.dek: LDraw-Nova is an open-source agent tool that generates 3D Lego models from natural language prompts.
top_news.brief: Powered by Astra and Opus 5.5, the agent translates user ideas into LDraw-compatible source code. The output includes 3D models, glTF files for Blender, and interactive VR support for Meta Quest 3, along with a full log of the agent's reasoning process.
top_news.image_alt: 3D rendered Lego model generated by AI

top_news.title: AI Gateway, Web Search API - Introducing Web Search API
top_news.dek: Cloudflare launches a beta Web Search API for AI agents to ground responses in real-time data.
top_news.brief: The API integrates with AI Gateway and supports providers including Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. All providers offer Zero Data Retention and adhere to verified bot crawling standards, enabling developers to bypass training cutoffs.
top_news.image_alt: Cloudflare Web Search API architecture diagram

top_news.title: Anthropic: Claude Frontier Academy: $100M to train 10,000 engineers
top_news.dek: Anthropic has launched the Claude Frontier Academy, a $100 million initiative to train 10,000 engineers in AI deployment by 2027.
top_news.brief: The program aims to bridge the enterprise AI talent gap by training Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) to the same technical standards used by Anthropic's internal teams. Initial cohorts include engineers from major firms like Accenture, Deloitte, McKinsey, and Morgan Stanley. The curriculum focuses on practical implementation skills required to deploy large-scale AI systems effectively.
top_news.image_alt: Anthropic Claude Frontier Academy logo and training program announcement graphic
